charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income

sections.title: Operating Drivers
sections.subtitle: Vehicle sales volumes and R&D spend are disclosed in the filings, not derived from financial lines

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For BYD Company Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For BYD Company Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For BYD Company Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For BYD Company Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For BYD Company Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For BYD Company Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For BYD Company Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For BYD Company Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

vehicleSales.title: Vehicle sales and NEV share
vehicleSales.content:
Total vehicle sales is units delivered in the period (BEV plus PHEV plus remaining ICE). NEV share is new-energy vehicles (BEV + PHEV) as a percentage of that total.

For BYD Company Limited: BYD has essentially completed its exit from ICE, so this chart is now mostly a volume-growth story rather than a mix-shift one. Domestic China NEV sales fell -32.7% YoY over the first 8 months of 2026 as Geely, Xiaomi, Leapmotor, Chery and Huawei-backed brands took share, even though BYD still led China retail NEV share at 23.3% in August 2026; September volumes rebounded +17% YoY.

What to watch:

  • Sequential volume trend, not just YoY (the China NEV market itself is decelerating from >60% penetration peaks)
  • Whether export volumes are offsetting domestic share loss
  • FY-only: monthly/quarterly sales bulletins outside the filings are the more current source

rnd.title: R&D expense and intensity
rnd.content:
R&D expense is spend on vehicle, battery and semiconductor development expensed in the period. R&D intensity is that spend as a percentage of revenue.

For BYD Company Limited: BYD's vertically-integrated model (in-house batteries, chips and now shipping) makes R&D intensity a direct read on whether it can keep undercutting rivals on cost while still improving the product -- the competitive edge the margin numbers above depend on.

What to watch:

  • R&D intensity holding up even as revenue growth slows -- a cut here would flag margin defence at the expense of the product pipeline
  • Absolute spend relative to Tesla and the domestic NEV rivals named in the competitive-position note

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For BYD Company Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
